critique.good: Every term stays on one line, making the shaded first column easy to scan. Definitions have comfortable line lengths, and the headers are clear.
critique.problems: Examples repeatedly run to five short lines, leaving noticeable unused space beneath several definitions. The term column is spacious relative to its brief labels.
critique.cause: The 173px term column preserves the longest label but leaves only 196px for examples; the 350px definition column is more generous than the example column.

critique.good: Examples have comfortable line lengths, and most term labels remain intact. The two prose columns have a consistent visual weight.
critique.problems: Definitions become dense blocks of five or six lines, while shorter examples leave large blank areas in the same rows. Eventual consistency wraps, so the term column does not fully preserve the scanning advantage of r0A.
critique.cause: At 290px, Definition has nearly the same width as Example despite holding substantially more text. The 140px term column is too narrow for the longest label.

critique.good: The wide definition column gives the primary explanations an open, readable rhythm. Words remain intact, and the narrow term column returns useful space to the prose.
critique.problems: Three multiword terms wrap, interrupting the scan down the row identifiers. Examples still form narrow, often five-line blocks, leaving blank space beneath some definitions.
critique.cause: The 120px term column provides only 99px of text space, while the 199px example column is much narrower than the 400px definition column.

critique.good: The term column is easy to scan, with only Eventual consistency wrapping. Definitions and examples generally form balanced, readable row units, and words remain intact.
critique.problems: The longer examples wrap to five lines, leaving some definitions shorter than their accompanying examples. Eventual consistency occupies two lines.
critique.cause: The 219px Example column is relatively narrow; the 140px Term column is too narrow for the longest label.

critique.good: All term labels fit on one line, making the first column especially easy to scan. Examples remain readable and words stay intact.
critique.problems: Definitions wrap more heavily, producing several tall rows and a six-line CAP theorem definition. The generous term column leaves conspicuous empty space below short labels.
critique.cause: The 173px Term column uses width that the 330px Definition column could use more effectively.

critique.good: The 380px Definition column gives the primary explanations comfortable lines, and words remain intact.
critique.problems: Both Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log wrap. Examples become narrow and ragged; the Write-ahead log example takes five lines, increasing its row height despite the wider definition.
critique.cause: The 130px Term and 209px Example columns have both been compressed to give Definition 380px.

critique.good: The term column is easy to scan, and the definition has enough width to read comfortably. Write-ahead log stays on one line, and words remain intact.
critique.problems: The Circuit breaker example ends with an isolated 'again' and makes the row taller than its definition requires. Eventual consistency wraps, but remains easy to recognize.
critique.cause: The 229px example column falls just short of a useful line-break threshold; the 140px term column is too narrow for Eventual consistency.

critique.good: The 234px example column gives Circuit breaker a more balanced four-line example, improving the row rhythm. Definitions remain readable and no words split mid-word.
critique.problems: Write-ahead log wraps after the hyphen, making the term list less uniform and slightly harder to scan. Some definition lines still end with short fragments, especially 'overload.'
critique.cause: The 135px term column is just too narrow for Write-ahead log. The 350px definition column leaves Backpressure at five lines.

critique.good: All term labels fit on one line, making the first column especially easy to scan. The definition column retains the same readable measure as the other designs.
critique.problems: Examples feel cramped and frequently determine row height. Quorum ends with an isolated 'nodes.' and Write-ahead log ends with 'checkpoint.', leaving noticeable unused space beneath shorter definitions.
critique.cause: The 173px term column reserves enough room for the longest label but reduces the example column to 196px.

understanding.purpose: Explain distributed-systems terminology through definitions and illustrative examples.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the first column for a term, read across to understand it, and use the example to make the concept concrete; taller definition cells can absorb some wrapping in the other columns.
groups: Definition and Example are complementary explanatory prose columns; Term is the row identifier and scanning anchor.
keep_intact: Individual words and any identifiers within the text
Term labels where practical, especially multiword terms
may_wrap: Definitions and examples at natural word boundaries
Multiword term labels when a narrower term column makes more room for explanations

bad.why: The oversized term column leaves substantial unused space in most rows, while the narrow definition column forces long explanations into many short lines and makes the table harder to scan.

contrast.why: The oversized term column leaves substantial unused space in most rows, while the narrow definition column forces long explanations into many short lines and makes the table harder to scan.

final.rationale: r2A gives definitions the most space while retaining a useful example column and a compact, easily scanned term column. Only one term wraps, and the longer definitions and examples generally occupy four or five lines without breaking words. The row boundaries keep each term, definition and example together, with a more balanced distribution of space than the wider-term alternatives.

general: Allocate width according to each column's role and content, while preserving enough space for row identifiers to be scanned.
Judge wrapping across whole rows: a shorter table is useful only when its text remains comfortable to read.
specific: Definitions need the largest share of this viewport, but examples also need enough width to read as short narratives.
Allowing 'Eventual consistency' to wrap frees space for both prose columns; keeping every term on one line makes the prose noticeably narrower.

final.tradeoffs: r2B is shorter and gives examples slightly more room, but also wraps 'Write-ahead log'. The wider-term designs keep every term on one line at the cost of narrower prose columns and taller rows.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative visual estimates, not browser-verified thresholds. A designer who prioritizes single-line row labels or more space for examples could reasonably choose a different candidate.

A.why: Terms stay on one line, but the wide term column leaves considerable empty space while definitions wrap into five to seven lines.

B.why: The generous definition column makes the main explanations easy to read, though two terms wrap and the narrower examples sometimes run to five lines.

C.why: Definitions and examples have balanced, readable widths, and only one term wraps. The quorum definition breaks the hyphenated phrase odd-sized across lines.

D.why: All terms remain on one line, supporting quick lookup, while definitions and examples have enough room to read comfortably. The rows feel coherent despite some longer definitions.

E.why: All terms fit on one line, but the equal columns give the short labels excessive space and squeeze definitions into many short lines.

F.why: Definitions and examples are well proportioned and rows scan easily, though two term labels wrap, including Write-ahead log.

reviews.unsure: C and F use the width efficiently; the preference for D depends on how much value the reader places on keeping every term on one line.

A.why: Definitions have comfortable line lengths and rows scan clearly, but the narrow term column wraps two labels and the examples are comparatively cramped.

B.why: Definition and example columns are well balanced, though two row labels wrap and the example for eventual consistency ends with a lone word.

C.why: All terms stay on one line, but the wide term column leaves substantial unused space while definitions wrap into tall blocks.

D.why: Every term stays on one line, while definitions and examples have useful, proportionate widths. Rows remain easy to scan across despite some longer definition blocks.

E.why: Nearly equal columns give the short terms excessive space and squeeze the longer definitions into narrow, tall blocks, leaving large empty areas in the other columns.

F.why: The definition and example columns read comfortably and most terms remain intact, but eventual consistency wraps and some rows have uneven text depths.

reviews.unsure: F is a close alternative if keeping definitions wider is more important than keeping every term on one line.
